page: Amazon Web Services t9g.medium is a burstable general-purpose cloud instance powered by AWS-engineered Graviton processors built on the arm64 architecture. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 2 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a rated clock frequency of 3.3 GHz. The hardware package supplies 4.0 GB of system memory, which yields an allocation of 2.0 GB per physical core.

The instance relies on a burstable CPU credit allocation rather than sustained continuous compute, making resource availability dependent on baseline utilization patterns. The platform does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating remote block storage solutions for operating system images and persistent data. Additionally, the instance features no graphics accelerators, provides a baseline network throughput of 0 Gbps, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Because of the energy-efficient Graviton architecture and burstable model, the t9g.medium offers strong cost efficiency for applications that experience variable or infrequent computational demands. Tradeoffs include throttled performance if CPU credit balances deplete under prolonged load, as well as dependence on network volumes for all file operations. The server is well positioned for lightweight workloads, such as software development environments, code compilation staging, low-traffic web serving, and intermittent background tasks.
